requirements.note: IBlockDevice::connect_client() creates/connects client channels.
Two per-client SPSC channels: ingress Command + callback Completion.
ReadSync/WriteSync with ns_id, DmaBuffer, LBA, no timeout.
Handle assigned at submission but only returned in the completion (fire-and-forget over channel); client correlates via caller tag, not the handle.
AbortOp only removes from pending_ops and acks; does not cancel the SPDK command. Client never receives the handle to abort a specific op (see FR-004).
WriteZeros via spdk_nvme_ns_cmd_write_zeroes.
BatchSubmit processes ops on a shared batch qpair.
NsProbe/NsCreate/NsFormat/NsDelete handled; namespace.rs helpers.
handle_controller_reset cancels all pending ops then resets and refreshes namespaces.
nvme_version (1.0.0), max_transfer_size (131072), and NUMA node (0) are hardcoded constants, not read from hardware. Capacity/sector/qd/io-queues are real.
min/max/mean latency, total ops, mean throughput; FeatureNotEnabled error without telemetry feature.
Single controller per instance via set_pci_address + initialize.
Actor NUMA-pinned, but controller NUMA node hardcoded to 0 at probe, so pinning always targets node 0.
poll_clients polls all attached client ingress channels.
STANDARD_DEPTHS [4,16,64,256], io_queue_requests=depth*4, shallowest-with-capacity, fallback most-available. Exact match.
ILogger receptacle wired; used throughout actor.
Uses spdk-env ISPDKEnv receptacle; checks is_connected before init.
Commands carry Arc<Mutex<DmaBuffer>> / Arc<DmaBuffer>.
Closed channel detected, client swap_removed, pending ops dropped, completions discarded.
Namespace ops dispatched serially on the actor thread.
IBlockDeviceAdmin: set_pci_address, set_actor_cpu, initialize, shutdown.
TscClock calibrated once at construction; timeout check throttled to ~1ms via TSC deadline.
ContextPool slab: acquire at submit, release in callback; allocates on first use, no full pre-alloc.
Reusable completion_scratch and timeout_scratch buffers.
ENOMEM retry to min(timeout_ms,1000).max(1); polls all qpairs each iteration; fails on deadline.
ClientSession::deliver/flush_pending non-blocking FIFO backlog; Completion derives Clone.
signal_stop closes channel without join; detach_controller drops parked controller.
on_stop drains (5s deadline) then delivers Error{Aborted} then parks controller; spec requires parking BEFORE the drain deadline is evaluated (order inverted, though actor loop already stopped).
Round-robin via rotating poll_start_idx; MAX_COMMANDS_PER_CLIENT_PER_POLL = 64 matches spec.
Sync read/write round-trip path present; latency envelope not statically verifiable.
Async timeout via TSC deadline with ~1ms throttle; bounded margin achievable.
Batch path routes to a shared qpair for aggregate throughput.
Full namespace lifecycle handled; refresh after each op.
Device info not fully hardware-consistent: version/max-transfer-size/NUMA are fixed constants regardless of the bound controller.
Telemetry records real TSC-derived latency (not hardcoded 0); accuracy within envelope.
Actor-vs-controller NUMA co-location not truly verified: controller NUMA node hardcoded 0, so guarantee degenerates to node 0.
Unit/doc tests present; perf coverage via benches + iops-benchmark app.
--op read/write/rw, default read.
--block-size default 4096.
--queue-depth default 32.
--threads default 1.
--duration default 10.
--ns-id default 1.
--pci-addr optional; uses first available device otherwise.
--pattern random/sequential, default random.
Validates block-size multiple-of-sector, threads/duration/queue-depth >= 1 before IO.
clamp_queue_depth to device max with warning.
Each worker calls ibd.connect_client() for its own channel pair.
Async pipeline kept full to configured queue depth.
rw mode uses rand::random::<bool>() for 50/50 read/write.
Config summary prints op, io-mode, pattern, block size(s), batch, queue depth, threads, duration, device, namespace.
Per-second progress to stderr with elapsed + instantaneous IOPS unless --quiet.
Timer sets stop_flag; workers joined and results collected.
Final summary: total IOPS, MB/s, latency min/mean/p50/p99/max in us.
rw mode reports read and write IOPS separately plus combined total.
RandomLba uniform within capacity; SequentialLba per-thread non-overlapping regions.
IO/timeout/error completions counted; thread continues.
exit 1 on validation failure, exit 2 on fatal, 0 on success.
--quiet suppresses progress output.
--help via clap derive.

--io-mode sync sends ReadSync/WriteSync but worker still pipelines to --queue-depth rather than enforcing effective QD1; QD1 realized only via actor-side serialization, and sync latency includes channel-queue wait.
Comma-separated --block-size list; each IO randomly picks one size.
--batch-size groups into BatchSubmit, but latency is measured per sub-op (one Instant + one completion each), not as aggregate latency per batch as the spec requires.
Worker NUMA pinning from device info (ibd.numa_node) via set_thread_affinity; excludes actor CPUs.
--device-count parallel multi-device init, threads*device_count workers, aggregate + per-device summary, pci-addr precedence, validate >=1.
Barrier-gated start + timer thread bound to duration.
Exactly one connect_client per worker thread (per device).
4KB random read path present; comparison to fio not statically verifiable.
Config validated across devices before any IO.
Progress computed from live per-thread op-counter deltas.

Latency stats computed correctly from actual completion times, but spec's telemetry cross-check is not wired: crate depends on block-device-spdk-nvme without the telemetry feature, so component telemetry() is unavailable.
IO errors counted in report without crashing or hanging.

unspecced.note: Per-direction read/write byte/op/latency counters not described in spec 001 (which specifies only aggregate telemetry).
Declared but unused in src/; production channels use component_core SpscChannel. Spec assumption flags cleanup via align-tasks.md.
Extra Criterion bench not referenced by SC-008.
Constraint not stated in spec-002 FR-024.
SPDK-init and device-init timing output not described in any FR.
